coverTitle:
Five Prayers
For The Work
That Feels Like Too Much
coverDek: For the job that takes more than it gives, the Sunday night dread, and the exhaustion nobody at the office can see — five prayers for the great work you're still doing, even when it's heavy.

points.hook: Lord, I don't remember the last time I talked about anything besides work.
paragraphs: We used to talk about other things — a book, a dream, a Saturday with nothing on it. Somewhere between the deadlines and the inbox that never empties, work became the only subject left in the room. Lord, give me back the parts of my life this job was never supposed to take.
points.verseText: Better is an handful with quietness, than both the hands full with travail and vexation of spirit.

points.hook: I decree over my labor: it will not be in vain.
paragraphs: I decree over every hour I give to this work: it will not be in vain, in the name of Jesus! Every project that feels unseen, every effort that feels unrewarded, I call it seed, not waste — and I declare that what I plant in obedience, heaven remembers. My labor is not lost, in Jesus' mighty name!
points.verseText: They shall not labour in vain.

points.hook: Notice what Sunday night does to your stomach before Monday even arrives.
paragraphs: Notice the knot that shows up Sunday evening, hours before the week even starts — your shoulders bracing, your sleep getting thinner, your body already working overtime on a day that's supposed to be rest. Lord, You never asked me to carry Monday on a Sunday. Loosen what my body is holding before the week even begins.
points.verseText: It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep.

points.hook: Somebody in this family is quietly burning out at a job that doesn't see them.
paragraphs: Somebody here is giving everything to a workplace that has never once said thank you, and they've stopped mentioning it because they think everyone's too busy to carry it with them. Family, bear one another's burdens — ask the quiet one at the back how the job is really going, and actually wait for the real answer.
points.verseText: Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.

points.hook: Child, I was there this morning when the alarm went off and you got up anyway.
paragraphs: Child, I was there this morning when the alarm went off and you got up anyway, even though nothing in you wanted to. Nobody at that job is going to applaud the parts only I saw — the patience you held onto, the integrity you kept when it would've been easier not to. I saw it all, and I am keeping a different kind of record than your manager does.
points.verseText: And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men; knowing that of the Lord ye shall receive the reward of the inheritance: for ye serve the Lord Christ.

cta.closingLine: If even one of these named what you carry into work every day, don't carry it alone — come back tomorrow for the next series.
